VecForge 2.0 gives Claude and other AI agents a long-term memory that stays on your machine, adds a local MCP server, fixes the quantum-inspired reranker, and makes the core faster and safer.

```bash
pip install --upgrade vecforge          # 2.0.0
pip install "vecforge[mcp]"             # with the MCP server for Claude
```

📕 **[Complete Instructions (PDF, 26 pages)](https://github.com/bosekarmegam/vecforge/blob/main/docs/VecForge-Instructions.pdf)** · 🌐 **[Website](https://bosekarmegam.github.io/vecforge/)** · 🎬 60-second intro reel attached below

Built by Suneel Bose K · ArcGX TechLabs Private Limited.

## What's new

### AI memory for Claude and other agents
- `MemoryStore` remembers facts, preferences, decisions, tasks and session summaries, and recalls them by relevance, importance and recency.
- Near-duplicate memories strengthen the existing one instead of piling up.
- Sessions with summaries, and `context_pack()` for a ready-made briefing at the start of a new chat.
- Each agent gets its own namespace, and memories can be exported and imported as JSON.

### Local MCP server
- `vecforge mcp` serves twelve memory and vault tools to Claude Desktop, Claude Code or any MCP client, over stdio or HTTP.
- `vecforge mcp --print-config claude-desktop` prints the exact config to paste.
- The embedding model loads in the background, and index snapshots are saved as you go, so the next session opens without a rebuild.

### Quantum-inspired rerank, corrected
- 1.x applied only the diffusion half of Grover's algorithm. That reversed the ranking for about half of all result-list sizes and did nothing for the rest.
- 2.0 implements the oracle and diffusion steps in closed form. Results that both the semantic and keyword retrievers found move up, and the best result always stays first.
- Measured at about 2 ms for a million candidates.

### Faster, more accurate core
- Incremental BM25 keyword index: adding a document no longer rebuilds the whole index.
- Namespace scoping and deletes now happen inside FAISS, so small namespaces keep full recall.
- Index snapshots stored in the vault: reopening skips the rebuild.
- Batched inserts, O(1) deletes with automatic compaction, and a `flat`, `hnsw` or `auto` index type.
- Pluggable embedders, including a hash embedder that needs no model download.

### Security
- Unregistered API keys now get no access (1.x gave read-only). Keys are stored as SHA-256 digests.
- `vecforge serve` listens on 127.0.0.1 by default.
- Writes are atomic: a failed index update rolls the rows back.
- Encrypted (SQLCipher) vaults open, back up and restore correctly.

## Upgrading from 1.x
- Existing vaults migrate automatically the first time you open them.
- `quantum_rerank=True` now returns the correct order, with scores from 0 to 1.
- Register API keys as admin before using them: `db.register_api_key(key, "read-only")`.
- `db.storage` (raw SQLite access) needs an admin key; `save()` and `compact()` need write access.
- Full list in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/bosekarmegam/vecforge/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Quality
- The full test suite (386 tests) passes on Linux, macOS and Windows with Python 3.10 to 3.13.
- 90% test coverage, and mypy strict, ruff and black are all clean.
- A randomized test compares every operation against a brute-force reference.
